findings.title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds a git submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` without a corresponding `.gitmodules` configuration. This looks like an accidentally committed nested git checkout and will break `git submodule` commands for anyone cloning the repository.

findings.title: Non-deterministic Python `hash()` used in shared cache key
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` build a shared cache key using `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. In Python 3, `hash()` is randomized per process via `PYTHONHASHSEED` (and can also produce collisions across different project ID tuples). Different worker processes will compute different cache keys for the same `(organization_id, project_ids)`, reducing cache hit rate across workers and making `invalidate_upsampling_cache` unable to reliably invalidate entries written by other processes. Use a deterministic representation (e.g., `','.join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))` or a hashlib digest) instead.

findings.title: `_get_event_stats` checks outer `dataset` and `request.GET` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query`
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` and `request` rather than the `scoped_dataset` and `query` parameters passed to `_get_event_stats`. During dashboard widget discover-splitting (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset = discover` and modified queries such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"` while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` / `metrics_performance`. Because `dataset` is not `discover` or `errors` (and `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET['query']` instead of the `query` argument), upsampling is either skipped on split error queries or could be misapplied if `request.GET['query']` contains `event.type:error` while executing the `event.type:transaction` split check.

findings.title: Substring check `"event.type:error" in query` matches negated or non-error queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` via a plain substring match on the raw query string. Queries such as `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, or a message/tag search containing the literal text `event.type:error` will match and cause `count()` to be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` (`sum(sample_weight)`) even though the query includes transaction or default events that do not have error `sample_weight`, producing incorrect counts.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling `NULL` or `0` weights for non-sampled events
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with the comment that `sample_weight` exists for all events in allowlisted projects. Even for an allowlisted project, historical events ingested before client error sampling was enabled, events from SDKs/clients that do not set `client_sample_rate`, or events where `sample_weight` is `NULL`/`0` will contribute `0` to `sum(sample_weight)` instead of `1` (e.g. `if(greater(sample_weight, 0), sample_weight, 1)` or ` coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`), causing `count()` to undercount or return `0` for unsampled events in allowlisted projects.
